notes: Verified the root cause: cmd/runtime-proxy/dlp.go:109 builds the log entry with "event":"dlp" and dlp.go:145 posts that entry verbatim under "event"; main's handler decoded it with DisallowUnknownFields, so every gateway report was a 400 ("받지 않는 항목입니다: \"event\"").

Ran the live test against a throwaway postgres:16 container (removed afterwards). On HEAD all 5 subtests pass. With internal/api/dlp.go swapped back to main's handler (only the new type/method stubs added so it compiles) 4 of 5 subtests fail with the 400 over the "event" key — the test genuinely pins the regression.

Unit test dlpreport_test.go cannot literally 'fail against the previous handler' as the commit message says: it calls decodePodReport, which does not exist on main, so it would be a compile error rather than a failing assertion. It does spell out the gateway's exact document, so a future shape drift is still caught. Cosmetic inaccuracy only.

The nothing_to_report 400 (internal/api/dlp.go:182) is safe: both record() call sites in cmd/runtime-proxy/dlp.go:77,82 only fire when Reportable() holds (findings non-empty or truncated), so no real gateway report is newly refused.
decodeJSON's behaviour for every other endpoint is unchanged (strict=true); leniency is limited to the token-authenticated dlp-events route.

Follow-up, out of scope: /runtime-gateway/tool-approvals and /runtime-gateway/config-report (internal/api/server.go:113,122) still use the strict decoder even though the decodePodReport comment's version-skew rationale applies to them too.

Live test leaves dlp.tool audit rows and one upserted owner user in the target DB (agents are deleted in cleanup); same pattern as the other *_live_test.go files, and it is opt-in via AGENTHUB_TEST_DSN.
